translationRepairs: Kerong eventually reached the posts of acting Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
Kerong eventually reached the posts of acting Minister of Works (Sikong) and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
司空 is Sikong/Minister of Works among the Three Dukes, not Grand Preceptor (太師).
Kerong rose in office to acting Grand Preceptor and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
Kerong rose in office to acting Minister of Works (Sikong) and Prince of Wuxing Commandery.
司空 is Sikong/Minister of Works, not Grand Preceptor (太師).
He repeatedly routed the rebel armies, and for his achievements was promoted to Grand Preceptor and advanced to the rank of Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia.
He repeatedly routed the rebel armies, and for his achievements was promoted to Minister of Works (Sikong) and advanced to the rank of Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia.
加司空 means promotion to Sikong/Minister of Works, not Grand Preceptor.
He repeatedly defeated rebel armies; for merit he was made Grand Preceptor and advanced to the Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia rank.
He repeatedly defeated rebel armies; for merit he was made Minister of Works (Sikong) and advanced to the Golden Pouch and Purple Regalia rank.
司空 is not Grand Preceptor.
In the third year of Taihe, After pacifying Cangzhou and Jingzhou he was made Grand Counselor in recognition of his merit and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.
In the third year of Taihe, after pacifying Cangzhou and Jingzhou he was made Grand Counselor in recognition of his merit and granted a substantive fief of three hundred households.
Spurious capitalization of After mid-sentence after the reign-year clause.
In the third year of Taihe, He pacified Cang and Jing; for his recorded merit he was made Grand Counselor and granted three hundred households of substantive fief.
In the third year of Taihe, he pacified Cang and Jing; for his recorded merit he was made Grand Counselor and granted three hundred households of substantive fief.
Spurious capitalization of He after the reign-year clause.
He was soon further honored as Grand Preceptor with privileges equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
He was soon further honored with the prestige rank of Kaifu Yitong Sansi (privileges equal to the Three Ducal Ministers).
開府儀同三司 is a prestige rank, not the office Grand Preceptor (太師).
Soon he was additionally made Grand Preceptor with the same honors as the Three Ducal Ministers.
Soon he was additionally granted Kaifu Yitong Sansi, with the same honors as the Three Ducal Ministers.
開府儀同三司 is not Grand Preceptor.
Zhongwu eventually reached the posts of Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor.
Zhongwu eventually reached the posts of Minister of Education (Situ) and Grand Counselor.
司徒 is Situ/Minister of Education, not Grand Mentor (太傅); the idiomatic rendering mistranslates the office.
Zhongwu rose in office to Grand Mentor and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
Zhongwu rose in office to Situ (Minister of Education) and Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
司徒 is mistranslated as Grand Mentor; literal English should preserve Situ/Minister of Education.
His son Zhifang — Zhifang — succeeded to his father's position as vice military governor of Youzhou.
His son Zhifang succeeded to his father's position as vice military governor of Youzhou.
The duplicated Zhifang mirrors a corrupted Chinese repetition and should not be retained in English.
Zhifang was reckless and violent by nature and committed acts of robbery and extortion; for repeated offenses he was demoted to defender of Liuzhou.
Zhifang was reckless and violent by nature and committed acts of robbery and extortion; for repeated offenses he was demoted to Sima of Liuzhou.
柳州司馬 is the office of Sima (administrator), not a defender.
Zhifang was by nature reckless and violent and committed acts of forcible seizure; for repeated offenses he was demoted to defender of Liuzhou.
Zhifang was by nature reckless and violent and committed acts of forcible seizure; for repeated offenses he was demoted to Sima of Liuzhou.
司馬 should be rendered Sima/administrator, not defender.
In the ninth year of Xiantong, He was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.

In the ninth year of Xiantong, he was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Situ (Minister of Education), concurrent Grand Mentor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.
檢校司徒 is acting Situ, not acting Grand Mentor; 太傅 is Grand Mentor. Also fix the stray capital He.
In the ninth year of Xiantong, He was cumulatively promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Mentor, concurrent Grand Preceptor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.
In the ninth year of Xiantong, he was cumulatively promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, acting Situ, concurrent Grand Mentor, Concurrent Grand Counselor, and Duke of Yan.
司徒 and 太傅 are misidentified in the English; 兼太傅 is concurrent Grand Mentor.
In the tenth year, when the people of Xu rebelled, Yunshen asked to send his younger brother Yunguo to lead troops against them, but Emperor Yizong refused.
In the tenth year, when the people of Xu rebelled, Yunshen asked to send his younger brother Yungao to lead troops against them, but Emperor Yizong refused.
允臯 is Yungao (臯 gao), not Yunguo; the English given name is a mistranscription.
In the tenth year the people of Xu rebelled; he requested that his younger brother Yunguo lead troops to suppress the rebellion, but Emperor Yizong did not approve.
In the tenth year the people of Xu rebelled; he requested that his younger brother Yungao lead troops to suppress the rebellion, but Emperor Yizong did not approve.
允臯 should be romanized Yungao, not Yunguo.
Before long Li Maoxun seized his position. Gongsu returned to the capital and was demoted to registrar of Fuzhou.
Before long Li Maoxun seized his position. Gongsu returned to the capital and was demoted to registrar of Fu Prefecture.
復州 is Fu Prefecture (not coastal Fuzhou 福州); the idiomatic rendering 'Fuzhou' invites the wrong place identification.
After the city fell, the Yan army grew somewhat overconfident.
After the city fell, the Yizhou soldiers grew somewhat overconfident.
Chinese 易州士卒 means the soldiers of/at Yizhou, not a generalized 'Yan army'; the idiomatic gloss invents Yan.
Chinese 可舉死 states only that Keju died; 'in the fighting' is an unsupported addition.
From afar they admired the righteousness of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were infected with the spirit of Lushan and Siming.
From afar they admired the righteousness of Tian Guang and Jing Ke; in recent times they were infected with the spirit of An Lushan and Shi Siming.
Literal English drops the surnames present in the idiomatic rendering and standard names for 祿山 and 思明, obscuring the referents.
The Li father and son for three generations perished within ten years.
The Li clan, father and sons across three generations, perished within ten years.
Literal English under-translates 李氏 and makes the three-generation clan-line sense harder to parse.
In the first year of Qianning, in winter Hedong heeded Rengong's plan and marched out to campaign against them.
In the first year of Qianning, in winter Hedong heeded Rengong's plan and marched out to campaign against Yan.
Literal 'against them' leaves the campaign target unspecified; following 燕軍 supports Yan.
